la:noun:condicio.gloss: An agreement, contract, covenant, stipulation, pact, proposition.
senses: An agreement, contract, covenant, stipulation, pact, proposition.
An external position, situation, rank, place, social status, circumstances, condition.
A nature, mode, character, disposition, manner, condition.
la:noun:condicio.html:
condĭcĭo (in many MSS. and edd. incorrectly condĭtĭo, and hence falsely derived from condo; cf. 2. conditio), ōnis, f.
condico
,
an agreement, stipulation, condition, compact, proposition, terms, demand.
Prop.
Absol.: alicui condicionem ferre,to offer terms,; cf. sq.; ; ; : cognitis suis postulatis atque aequitate condicionum perspectā,; : non respuit condicionem,; so : ne si pax cum Romanis fieret, ipse per condiciones ad supplicium traderetur,: condiciones pacis, quas adfertis, si accepero,: posse condicionibus bellum poni,: dum de condicionibus tractat,: his condicionibus conpositā pace,: aliquot populos aut vi subegit aut condicionibus in societatem accepit,: ex quā condicione,in consequence of,: sub condicionibus eis pacem agere,: accipe sub certā condicione preces,: sub condicione,conditionally, Weissenb. ad loc.; usu. without a prep.: eā enim condicione acceperas,: eādem condicione,; ; ; : istā quidem condicione,: nullā condicione,: ullā condicione,: his legibus, his condicionibus erit quisquam tam stultus, etc.,.—
With ut or ne: fert illam condicionem, ut ambo exercitus tradant, Cael. ap. : eā accepisse condicione, ut, etc.,: hac condicione, ut, etc.,; ; ; : jubere ei praemium tribui sed eā condicione, ne quid postea scriberet, B. and K.: permisit eā solā condicione, ne, etc.,: fecit pacem his condicionibus: ne qui, etc.,; so ; —
With si (rare; not in Cic.): librum tibi eā condicione daret, si reciperes te correcturum, Caecin. ap. ; ; ; .—
With dum (rare): jam vero istā condicione, dum mihi liceat negare, etc.,.— Also transf. subject., free choice, option: quorum condicio erat,who had their choice,.—From the conditions made in marriage,
Esp., a marriage, match; sometimes, by meton., = the person married (freq. and class.).
In an honorable sense, in full: condicio uxoria,; usu. alone: tu condicionem hanc accipe; ausculta mihi, Atque eam desponde mihi,; so ; : ut eam in se dignam condicionem conlocem,: hanc condicionem si quoi tulero extrario,: aliam quaerere,: condicionem filiae quaerendam esse,; : alicui deferre,; ; ; ; ; ; .—Hence, in the jurists, the formula of separation: condicione tuā non utor,I will not have you,. —
In a bad sense, an amour, the relation of lover or mistress: accepit condicionem, dein quaestum occipit,; cf.: quae tibi Condicio nova, luculenta, fertur per me,; and hence, meton., a lover, paramour: habeo hortos ... hinc licet condiciones cottidie legas,; ; ; .—
In gen., the external position, situation, condition, rank, place, circumstances (very freq. and class.).
Of persons: est haec condicio liberorum populorum. etc.,: condicio infirma et fortuna servorum,; cf.: tolerabilis servitutis,: condicione eo meliore est senex quam adulescens,: humana,: ista condicio est testium, ut quibus creditum non sit negantibus, eisdem credatur dicentibus,: alia oratoris,; : alicujus condicio vitaque,: abjectae extremaeque sortis. 35: fuit intactis quoque cura condicione super communi, solicitude concerning their common condition or circumstances, ; ; ; ; .—
Of things, a situation, condition, nature, mode, manner: quae consuerint gigni gignentur eādem Condicione,: agri,: frumenti,: aliquam vitae sequi, mode or manner of living, : earum (frugum) cultus et condiciones tradere, B. and K.; cf.: haec vivendi,: diversa causarum inter ipsas,: duplex ejus disceptationis,: litium,; cf. : vel temporum vel locorum, et saep.

la:verb:conduco.gloss: to lead, bring or draw together; assemble, collect
senses: to lead, bring or draw together; assemble, collect
to connect, join, unite; close up; coagulate
to hire, rent, employ, take on lease, undertake; farm; bribe
to be conducive to, contribute to something by being useful, to be of use or profitable, serve
la:verb:conduco.html:
con-dūco, xi, ctum, 3, v. a. and n.
Act., to draw, bring, or lead together, to assemble, collect (class. in prose and poetry).
In gen.
Of persons (esp. freq. of the collecting, assembling of troops in any place): milites de castellis ad castra, Sisenn. ap. : populum in forum,: exercitum in unum locum,: eo copias omnes,: copias suas,; cf. auxilia,; : dispersas suorum copias,: virgines unum in locum,: omnis clientes suos eodem,: milites in unum,; cf. .—
Of inanimate objects: vineas,: nubila, —
Esp.,
Intens., to connect, unite, by bringing together, = cogo, colligo.
Prop. (so several times in Lucr., elsewhere rare): partes in unum,; ; cf. ; ; : cortice ramos,: lac,to coagulate, curdle,: conducere musculum aut laxare,to contract,, n. 8: ubi sunt nervi, interiores conducunt membra,: vulnera cerā,to close up,—
Trop.: propositionem et assumptionem in unum,; cf. : omnia probra in deorum maledicta,: dies adeo conductus,i. e. short,.—
T. t. of the lang. of business, to hire, take on lease, to farm (correlative of locare; cf. ; very freq. and class.).
To hire for one's use, to hire, rent, employ; of things: aedes aliquas mihi,; ; cf.: domum in Palatio,

; : hortum,: qui colonus habuit conductum de Caesenniā fundum,: habitationem in annum,: ad certum tempus,: insulam,: conduxi domum a te,: nummos,to borrow,; cf. pecuniam,.—Esp., of persons: ille qui me conduxit, ubi conduxit, abduxit domum,: cocum, and 15; : fidicinam, quae cantaret sibi,: meretricem,; cf. ; Nep. praef. § 4; and poet.: torum,: consulem vestrum ad caedem faciendam,: praeceptores publice,: choragum,: homines,; so, militem (the Gr. ξενολογεῖν), to hire soldiers, ; ; cf. the foll. subst.—With ut or quin: aliquem uti taceat, to hire, bribe, employ, Cato ap. ; cf.: tribus non conduci possim libertatibus, quin, etc.,could not be hired,; cf. Lucil. ap. : mercede aliquem,: mercede diurnā conductus,: pictorem magno pretio,.—Subst.

conducti, ōrum, m., hirelings, mercenary soldiers, ; ; cf. ; ; —Hence, poet.: bella conducta,carried on by mercenary troops,. —
conductum, i, n., any thing hired, esp. a house, dwelling, etc., ; ; ; ; cf.: locati conducti, tit.: actio ex conducto, an action upon a lease or contract, , §§ 4 and 8 al.—
To undertake any service (building, transportation, the customs, etc.), to contract for, farm: caedundum illum (agnum) ego conduxi,; cf.: caedundos agnos,: redemptor, qui columnam illam de Cottā conduxerat faciendam,: locare faciendum quod ego conduxeram,; so, mulierem vehendam nave,: aliquem docendum,; : praebenda, quae ad exercitum opus essent,to undertake the supplies,: vectigalia,to farm,; : tabulas in Italiam portandas,; so, portorium, —
Neutr., to contribute to something by being useful, to be of use or profitable, to profit, serve, etc. (syn.: convenit, utile est; class.; used only in the 3d pers. of the sing. and plur.); constr. with in, ad aliquid, the dat., or absol.
With in: quod tuam in rem bene conducat,; so, maxime in rempublicam, Sisenn. ap. : in commune,.—
With ad: ad ventris victum,: ad vitae commoditatem,.—
With dat. (so most freq.): huic aetati non conducit latebrosus locus,: maxime rei publicae,; : neque homini infanti injuste facta conducunt,; : omnibus,: tuae laudi,: nostris rationibus,: maxime sibi,: alvo citae (vinum),: proposito, et saep.: imbres non conducunt vitibus,.—
Absol.: dubitare non possumus. quin ea maxime conducant, quae sunt rectissima,: conducere arbitror talibus auris tuas vocibus undique circumsonare,.—Hence, P. a. as subst.; v. I. C. 2. βfin. supra.— Adv.: condūcenter, becomingly, fitly, .
la:verb:conduco.inflection: xi, ctum, 3, v. a. and n.

la:noun:conductor.html:
conductor, ōris, m.
conduco
,
one who hires a thing, a lessee, farmer, tenant, a contractor (rare, and mostly absol.): (histrionum),: (pecoris),: (agri),; ; cf. : (aedificii),: operis,: sacrae arae,, ext. 1: ; ; ; cf. .

la:verb:condio.html:
condĭo, īvi or ĭi, ītum, 4, v. a.
an access. form from condo, q. v. II., and cf. compono, II. B. 2.
(orig. belonging to econ. lang.).
To put fruit in vinegar, wine, spices, etc., to preserve, pickle: oleas albas,: lactucam (corresp. with componere),; : corna, pruna,: caules vitium in aceto et muriā,—
Transf.
Unguenta, to make fragrant, .—
To embalm a dead body: mortuos (Aegyptii),.—
Of food, to make savory, to season, spice: cenam,: meas escas,: fungos, helvellas, herbas omnes ita, ut nihil possit esse suavius,: jus male conditum,: vinum,; cf.: quis non videt, desideriis omnia ista condiri?.—Hence,
As subst.: con-dītum, i, n. (sc. vinum), aromatic wine, spiced wine, ; ; ; —
Trop., to cultivate, ornament; to make pleasant or agreeable; to soften, temper, etc. (freq. in Cic.): duo sunt, quae condiant orationem: verborum numerorumque jucunditas,; cf. ; and 6, 3, 40: vitia,to set off,: hilaritate tristitiam temporum,: gravitatem comitate,; cf. : aliquid natura asperum pluribus voluptatibus,: urbanitatem ambiguitate,. —Hence, condītus, a, um, P. a.
(Acc. to II. A.) Seasoned, savory: conditiora facit haec supervacanei etiam operis aucupium atque venatio,: sapor vini,.—
Trop. (acc. to II. B.), of discourse, polished, ornamented: sermo, Poët. ap. : nimium condita oratio,.— Comp.: oratio lepore et festivitate conditior,; . —Of the speaker: nemo suavitate conditior,.—Sup. and adv. not in use.
la:verb:condio.inflection: īvi or ĭi, ītum, 4, v. a.

senses: to build, establish; form, fashion; make, construct
to put away, store or treasure up; preserve; inter, bury
to conceal, hide, secret, suppress, withdraw
to thrust or strike in deep, plunge
to bring to an end, conclude
la:verb:condo.html:
con-do, dĭdi, dĭtum, 3, v. a.
con- = cum, and 2. do
, lit.,
to bring, lay or put together (very freq. in all periods and species of composition).
With the access. idea of uniting, to put or join together into a whole, to form, fashion, produce, make by joining together.
Prop., of the founding of towns or states, to found, establish: Romam, Enn. ap. , and (Ann. v. 494 Vahl.): oppida,; : urbem,; ; ; ; ; ; ; : arces,: locum,: colonias. ; : civitatem,: regna,: imperium Poenorum,.—Hence, often ante and post Romam conditam, before and after the foundation of Rome, ; cf. Liv. praef. § 6 al.—
Transf. to the inhabitants: Romanam gentem,: genus hominum,.—Hence, mid.: optato conduntur Thybridis alveo,they settle, (condi proprie dicuntur, qui sibi statuunt civitatem. Conduntur ergo; sedem stabilem locant, Serv.). —
Of the erecting, building of other things, to make, construct, build: aram,; : sepulcrum,: moenia,; ; ; .—
Of written productions, to compose, write, celebrate, write or treat of, describe: SIVE CARMEN CONDIDISSET, Fragm. XII. Tab. ap. ; so, carmen,; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.: poëma,: longas Iliadas,: bella,: Caesaris acta,: proelia,: festa numeris,: alterum satirae genus,: aliqua in hac materiā,: prosam orationem,: historiam,; cf.: aliquid annalibus,: praecepta medendi,: laudes alicujus,.— Rarely,
Absol.: si etiamnum Homero condente Aegyptus non erat,.—
Trop., to establish, found, to be the author of, to produce, make: jusjurandum,: aurea saecula,: collegium novum,: morem,: nova fata,: aeternam famam ingenio suo,; so, nomen memorandum,: militarem disciplinam artemque bellandi,: somniorum intellegentiam (Joseph),.—Of the gods: portenta sua,to fuifil, accomplish,.—Impers.: naturā rerum conditum est, ut, etc.,.—
With the access. idea of carefulness, to put away, to lay, put, or place somewhere for preservation, etc.; to lay up, store or treasure up (opp. promo).
In gen.
Prop.
Aliquid: pecuniam,: frumentum,; : condere et reponere fructus,

: agri multa efferunt, quae ... mandentur condita vetustati,; cf. ; ; Auct. B. Afr. 65: vinum,; cf. ; ; : aliquid proprio horreo,: Sabinum testā levi,: pressa mella puris amphoris,: messem,: fruges,.—

With the designation of the place (most freq. by in and acc.): minas viginti in crumenam,: mustum in dolium,: cineres in urnas,: barbam in auream pyxidem,; cf. : legem in aerarium,: libri in sacrarium conditi,; cf. the foll.: te in pistrinum,; cf.: aliquem in custodiam,; : aliquem in carcerem,to thrust into prison, imprison,; ; ; ; 45, 42, 5: aliquem in vincula,; . —With adv.: argentum intro,; : sortes eo, Orell. N. cr.—With in and abl.: litteras publicas in aerario sanctiore,to keep, lay up,: se (aves) in foliis,: novissimo die dein (argyritin) condunt in plumbeo vase,.—With abl.: condidit (libros Sibyllinos) duobus forulis auratis sub Palatini Apollinis basi,; .—With locat.: id domi nostrae,; cf.: ut ei jam exploratus et domi conditus consulatus videretur,i. e. he was sure of it,.—
Trop.: teneo omnia; in pectore condita sunt,: mandata corde memori,: tu, qui omne bonum in visceribus medullisque condideris,: in causis conditae sunt res futurae,lie, are contained,. —Hence,
Esp.,
In econom. lang., to preserve, pickle (for which the access. form condio, īre, became prevalent): lentiscum in acetum (cf. just before, oleae quomodo condiantur),: ficus in orcas,: fructum in cados,: corna in liquidā faece,: oleum,.—
In medic. lang., to set: ossa,: calcem,: articulum,.—
To inter, bury (cf. compono, II. B. 1. c.): mortuos cerā circumlitos,: aliquem sepulcro,; ; ; : ossa parentis terrā,; so, aliquem terrā,: corpora defunctorum in lapide sarcophago,: fraternas umbras tumulo,; so ; : ossa peregrinā ripā,: in Tomitanā condar humo?: inhumatos Manes,: Alexandrum intemperantiā bibendi ... condidit,brought to the grave,: patrem,: fulgura publica condere,, v. fulgur; cf.: Aruns dispersos fulminis ignes Colligit et terrae maesto cum murmure condit,—
Poet., of time, to pass, spend, live through, bring to a close: saecla vivendo,: longos soles cantando,: cum referetque diem condetque relatum,i. e. morning and evening,: diem collibus in suis,: diem,; ; ; : noctem,.—In respect to lustrum, v. 2. lustrum, I.—
Transf., to conceal, hide, secrete, suppress: Sibyllam quidem sepositam et conditam habeamus, ut ... injussu senatūs ne legantur quidem libri,: quicquid sub terrā est in apricum proferet aetas, Defodiet condetque nitentia,: lumen,; so, lunam (nubes),: aliquid jocoso furto,: vultus,; cf.: vultum aequore,: enses,to sheathe,: ferrum,: gladium,: scuta latentia,: oculos,to close, shut, (but oculi conditi, v. P. a. infra); so, lumina,se in viscera (terrae),: se sub lectum,.—Mid., : nocte ... aliquot Numidarum turmas medio in saltu condiderat,i. e. placed in ambush,; so, hostis in silvis armatum militem condidit, ; cf.: ibi Dahas condidit,: (Danai) notā conduntur in alvo,concealed themselves,: fera murmura,iram,.—With abl.: his mensibus pisces jacent speluncis conditi,: huic sollertiā est inanium ostrearum testis se condere,: luna condita tenebris,: aliquid alvo,to swallow,.—
Poet.
To thrust or strike in deep, to plunge (cf. abscondo): ensem in pectus,: digitos in lumina,; 12, 295; 5, 423: ensem totum alicui in adverso pectore,: telum jugulo,; ; cf. pass.: nihil tam facile in corpus quam sagitta conditur,, n. 2.—
Trop.: stimulos caecos in pectore,.—
To hide by sailing away, to lose sight of: navita condit urbes,; cf. abscondo.—Hence,
condĭtus, a, um, P. a., close, secret, deep (rare): praecordia,: oculi,deep set,.—
condĭta, ōrum, n., the laid up store (late Lat.), Cod. Th. 7, 4, 3;

la:verb:condoleo.gloss: to feel severe pain, suffer greatly
senses: to feel severe pain, suffer greatly
to suffer with or feel another's pain; condole
la:verb:condoleo.html:
con-dŏlĕo, ēre,
v. n., to feel severe pain, to suffer greatly (eccl. Lat.).
Universum corpus, .—
Trop.: animo,, n. 12.—
To suffer with another, to feel another's pain; with dat.: qui non condolent proximis suis, sed potius eos irrident, Aug. in Job, 19, 13; ; .

la:verb:condico.gloss: to talk something over together, agree to/upon, concert, promise; fix, appoint
senses: to talk something over together, agree to/upon, concert, promise; fix, appoint
to give notice that something should be returned, demand back
la:verb:condico.html:
con-dīco, xi, ctum, 3, v. a.
To talk a thing over together, to agree upon, to concert, to promise (most freq. as publicists' t. t.): condixit pater patratus populi Romani Quiritium patri patrato priscorum Latinorum, etc., old form ap. : status condictusve dies cum hoste, Cincius ap. ; ; cf.: quoniam pactum atque condictum cum rege populi Romani perfide ruperat,: sic constituunt, sic condicunt,: inducias,: tempus et locum coëundi,: ruptā quiete condictā,the truce,: in diem tertium,: in vendendo fundo quaedam etiam si non condicantur praestanda sunt,.—*
Trop.: cum hanc operam (scribendi) condicerem, obligated myself to it, i. e. undertook it, Plin. praef. § 6 Jan.—Hence,
Esp.
To proclaim, announce, publish: condicere est dicendo denuntiare, Paul. ex Müll.; cf.: sacerdotes populi Romani cum condicunt in diem tertium, diem perendini dicunt,.—
Condicere alicui ad cenam or cenam, to engage one's self as guest at an entertainment: ad cenam aliquo condicam foras,; : seni cenam eā lege condixit,; cf.: velut ad subitam condictamque cenulam invitare,i. e. without previous preparation,.—Absol.: nam cum mihi condixisset, cenavit apud me in mei generi hortis,: ad balneas,.—
In the jurists: condicere aliquid alicui, lit., to give notice that something should be returned; hence, to demand back, make a formal claim of restitution (from any one): rem,: pecuniam alicui,; or for satisfaction: quia extinctae res, licet vindicari non possunt, condici tamen furibus et quibusdam aliis possessoribus possunt, Gai ; cf. , and v. condictio and condicticius.—
In late Lat., to assent or agree unanimously, = consentire, ; ; .

la:verb:condemno.gloss: to condemn, convict, sentence. (+ genitive or + ablative of the crime, + ad + accusative of the punishment)
senses: to condemn, convict, sentence. (+ genitive or + ablative of the crime, + ad + accusative of the punishment)
la:verb:condemno.html:
con-demno, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
damno
.
To sentence, condemn, convict (in good prose; rare in the poets).
In judicial proceedings (opp. absolvo); constr. aliquem, with gen., abl., de aliquā re, later with ad or in aliquid, or with ut.
Aliquem: hunc per judicem condemnabis, cujus de eā re nullum est arbitrium?; : Scamandrum, Fabricium,: qui cum judex esset, pecuniam acciperet ab accusatore ut reum condemnaret,: omnis de consilii sententiā,, § 114: aliquem judicio turpissimo,: ceteros causā incognitā,: L. Murenam,: super quadraginta reos ex diversis criminibus una sententia,: aliauem multā inrogatā, et

saep.: hunc hominem Veneri absolvat, sibi condemnat,for his own benefit,; cf.: illum libertum illi patrono HS. X. milia condemnare, i. e. to pay him, Gai .—Pass. with kindr. acc.: quasi ei, qui magnā fide societatem gererent, arbitrium pro socio condemnari solerent,in an arbitration on the partnership,: quidquid hereditario nomine condemnatus esset, Gai .—And in jurid. formulae, also in act. with acc. of that to or in which one is condemned or mulcted: judex, si condemnat, certam pecuniam condemnare debet, Gai ; : usuras usurarum,.—

With acc. and gen.: aliquem ambitūs,; : aliquem capitis,capitally,; : injuriarum,: pecuniae publicae,: rerum capitalium,: sponsionis,: voti, obliged to fulfil his vow (because his wish was granted), Titin. ap. (Com. Rel. v. 153 Rib.); Turp. ib. (Com. Rel. v. 128 ib.); cf.: damnare voti,.—
With acc. and abl.: aliquem eodem crimine,: actionibus famosis,: capitali poenā,: certā pecuniā,to a certain sum,; cf.: minori pecuniā,.—
Acc. and de aliquā re: aliquem de aleā,: de ambitu,.—(ε) Acc. and ad aliquid: aliquem ad metalla, et munitiones viarum aut bestias,; cf.: ad bestias,: ad mortem,; : ad pecuniam,.—(ζ) Acc. and in aliquid: in antliam,: in solidum,: in certam quantitatem,.— (η) Acc. and ut: condemnatus, ut pecuniam solvat,.—

la:verb:condono.html:
con-dōno, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
Aliquid (aliquem) alicui, to give something to one, to present, deliver up (in good prose; most freq. in Cic.; not in Quint.).
In gen.
Prop.: pallam,: pateram tibi,: apothecas hominibus nequissimis,: omnia certis hominibus (corresp. with dare),: facultas agrorum suis latronibus condonandi, Wernsd. N. cr. (cf. Zumpt, Gram. § 661): hereditatem alicui (praetor),to adjudge,.—
Trop., to give up, surrender, deliver up, sacrifice, devote, bring as an offering: aliquid dicioni, judicio potestatique alicujus permittere et condonare,: aliquid potentiae alicujus,: consuli totam Achaiam,: aliquem cruci,: omnes inimicitias rei publicae,: ne patiamini M. Caelium libidini muliebri condonatum,: ut M. Aemilius cum suā dignitate omni ... vanissimae genti condonetur, ; cf.: seque vitamque suam reipublicae,: suum dolorem ejus voluntati ac precibus,.—
Esp., to give a debt to one, i. e. to remit, acquit from.
Prop.: pecunias creditas debitoribus,.—More freq.,
Trop.
To pardon, remit an offence: ut crimen hoc nobis condonetis,: uti Jugurthae scelus condonaretur,.—
To pardon, refrain from punishing a crime out of regard or favor: meam animadversionem et supplicium, quo usurus eram in eum, remitto tibi et condono, Vatin. ap. : alterius lubidini malefacta condonare,: tres fratres non solum sibi ipsis, neque his tot ac talibus viris, neque nobis necessariis suis, sed etiam rei publicae condonaveris,: non sibi ac defensioni suae condonatum esse Oppianicum,: datus est tibi ille, condonatus est ille,; : filium sibi,: unum tot Claudiis deprecantibus,: Divitiaco fratri (sc. Dumnorigem),—
Aliquem aliquid or absol., to present one with something (only in the foll. exs.): si quam (rem) debes, te condono,; so : argentum, quod habes, condonamus te,: aurum aliquem, Afran. ap. .—Pass. impers., with acc. of thing: habeo alia multa quae nunc condonabitur,.
